title: CoLaX: Context-Aware Local Explanations for Time Series Classification
claim: Explanations that score local patterns in isolation are ambiguous, because identical patterns carry different meaning under different global contexts.
layout: 2 panels side-by-side; left shows the baseline, right shows the challenge with dashed links
description: Two panels of black wiggly time-series curves with colored highlighted segments. Panel (a), "Local-Prototype-only explanation", shows three small boxed prototypes (LP-1 blue, LP-2 yellow, LP-3 orange) at the top. Dashed lines link each prototype to its matching segment in one long series in a black frame below. Panel (b), "Challenge: Ambiguity without global context", stacks two series. The top series has a flat red dashed trend and the bottom series has a downward-sloping red dashed trend. The same blue, yellow and orange prototype windows appear in both, joined by dashed lines and labeled "Same local prototype". Gray curved arrows labeled "Conditions" and "Global context conditions local prototypes" show the context acting on the prototypes. Black arrows on the right point to a red dashed box reading "Distinct global contexts". The eye goes first to the colored windows.
caption: Ambiguity of local prototype explanations without global temporal context. (a) Local-pattern–only explanation. Local prototypes (LP-1 to LP-3) capture discriminative motifs but implicitly assume that their contributions are invariant across contexts. (b) Context-dependent ambiguity under distinct global temporal structures. Identical local patterns may appear under distinct global temporal structures. Their contributions should be interpreted as conditional on the global context, motivating the need for context-aware explanation frameworks.
abstract: Post-hoc explanations for time series classifiers usually score local patterns, such as subsequences or shapelets, without regard to the rest of the sequence. Yet the same motif can carry different predictive meaning under different global temporal conditions, such as trends or regimes. We propose CoLaX, a context-aware post-hoc explanation framework that builds on shapelet-driven Shapley attribution and conditions local-pattern relevance on a learned representation of the full sequence. Global context acts at two levels: it produces sample-specific prototype weights and a temporally resolved signal that reweights the local activation map. The resulting context-conditioned segments are the players of a Shapley attribution game whose values come only from the frozen black-box classifier. On synthetic benchmarks where identical motifs change relevance across contexts, CoLaX improves AUPRC over the strongest baseline by 30\% on average. On real-world data, it achieves the highest AUPRC on ECG. Additional ablations indicate that the gains come from input-dependent conditioning rather than from additional learnable weights. CoLaX is therefore most useful when recurring local motifs change relevance across sequence-level contexts.
